text:
Cole Caufield scored 51 goals last season and won the Lady Byng, and he has 12 more through 21 games. Against Boston on Nov. 12 he became, as 98.5 The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson posted, "the first player to have a 12 goals in 12 games stretch against the Bruins since Auston Matthews."

The shot is genuine. He has 69 shots and 8.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.9 scoring chances per 60 from the slot last season, 97th percentile. Only nine skaters have added more wins with their goals this season.

But our numbers flag him as due to cool. Twelve goals on 8.7 expected is shooting 17%, and Montreal has scored 5.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. At five on five his line is getting only 47.3% of the expected goals, 4.7 points worse than the team without him. That is the part to watch: last season Evolving-Hockey had his chances running well ahead of his results, and this season it has flipped.

Over his last ten he has 9 points, right around the 9.4 we'd expect.
